disease_label_per_paper: Relapsing polychondritis in a liver transplant recipient with auricular and nasal cartilage inflammation
presentation_summary: 59-year-old male liver transplant recipient for primary sclerosing cholangitis, with ulcerative colitis and ongoing post-transplant immunosuppression, developed rhinitis followed by painful swelling and redness of the left auricle.
On admission the left ear cartilage was swollen, red, hot, and painful with sparing of the earlobe; nasal cartilage involvement presented as pressure tenderness of the nasal base.
Scintigraphy/SPECT-CT showed increased marker accumulation in auricles and nasal septum; other organ involvement workup was negative.
Labs showed WBC 13.6 G/L, neutrophils 9.16 G/L, ESR 86 mm/hr, CRP 97.3 mg/L, hypergammaglobulinemia, and normal liver/kidney function.
External ear cultures grew Klebsiella oxytoca and Candida albicans, but antibiotics and prednisone 15 mg did not stop progression; right auricle inflammation developed.

After excluding infection, PTLD, and malignancy, methylprednisolone pulses followed by high-dose oral steroids and azathioprine improved inflammation and labs; later ear cartilage loss and saddle-nose deformity were observed.

actual_treatment: clindamycin, amoxicillin, and lincomycin before diagnosis
intravenous antibiotics for external ear isolates
prednisone dose increased to 15 mg/day then 30 mg/day
actual_outcome: Local cartilage inflammation, general condition, and laboratory results improved with intensified immunosuppression.
Significant ear cartilage loss and saddle-nose deformity were present after acute symptoms remitted.
Control scintigraphy/SPECT showed very good treatment response.
quality_warnings: Scintigraphy, biopsy, diagnostic criteria, and treatment response are confirmatory and marked use_in_ranking:false.
External ear microbiology is retained as infection/mimic context rather than deleted.
Exact kidney/liver lab values were not reported; only normal kidney function was encoded qualitatively with an approximate normal creatinine warning.
